target: Let E be a real normed space with its original arbitrary norm, V a nonempty set, n a natural number and lambda>=0. Let psi:E to R be lambda-strongly convex on V. For every i<n, assume loss_i:E to EReal is never bottom anywhere, is below top on V, and its real restriction is convex on V. Define F(x)=psi(x)+sum_{i<n} loss_i(x)+I_V(x), using ordinary extended-real addition and I_V=0 on V/top outside. Then F is proper, dom(F)=V, F equals the real sum on V, and F satisfies the exact lambda/2 strong interpolation inequality on V. Convexity of V follows from the regularizer hypothesis. The theorem assumes no property of the resulting F. This is a derived sufficient-condition producer, not the full numbered source theorem. Regularizer-supplied curvature and convex component losses are stronger than assuming curvature of the total objective in Lemma7.5/7.47/15.31. Algorithm15.9 already prints a common-domain condition; common finiteness is a restriction relative to broader extended-real Algorithm7.1 branches, not a newly discovered omission there. Algorithm7.1 has psi:X to R with V subset X, while Corollary7.6 uses psi:V to R; arbitrary real extension outside V has no effect after the indicator. The below-top domain condition alone admits bottom; separate global no-bottom makes the included losses finite on V and prevents mixed-infinity addition. Zero n and zero lambda are allowed. No minimizer, support, finite-dimensionality, strict curvature, closedness or attainment is assumed or produced.
